ux.screen: Settings (full page) vs Project settings modal
ux.purpose: Configure the whole site — identity, SEO, distribution and plumbing — from one place.
ux.finding: There are two site-settings surfaces with overlapping fields and no link between them. The rail's Settings is a full-page surface with 13 sections. The Site menu's 'Site settings' and the Cmd+, shortcut open a different thing — a three-tab modal (General / Canvas / SEO) that edits project name, author, grid size, snap-to-grid and the social site name. Project name and SEO site name are editable in both. A user who changes the name in one has no way to know the other exists, and the two use different save models (modal discard-confirm vs the panel's sticky savebar).
ux.evidence: ProjectSettingsModal.tsx:41-45 TABS general/canvas/seo, :166-241 the fields, :262 its own 'Discard these settings?' confirm. AquibraStudio.tsx:366 openSiteSettings: modals.openProjectSettings and :508 onOpenProjectSettings; useEditorShortcuts.ts:119-123 Cmd+',' -> openSiteSettings. SettingsTab.tsx:75-92 the 13-row NAV; tabsConfig.ts:187-199 the rail entry (shortcut S, mode fullpage). Searched: 'ProjectSettingsModal', 'openProjectSettings', 'openSiteSettings', 'Site settings'.
ux.fix: One home for site configuration. Fold Canvas (grid/snap) into the full-page Settings as a 'Canvas' section, point Cmd+, and the Site menu at it, and delete the modal.

ux.purpose: Configure the whole site — identity, SEO, distribution and plumbing — from one place.
ux.task: Remove a redirect I no longer need
ux.finding: Deleting a redirect fires the server mutation on the first click. No confirm, no undo, no toast. A redirect is a live routing rule that search engines and existing inbound links depend on — deleting the wrong row silently 404s traffic, and the only feedback is the row disappearing.
ux.evidence: RedirectsScreen.tsx:160-168 handleDelete -> getClient().siteDetail.redirects.delete.mutate({ id }) with no guard; the trigger at :249-258 is a plain Button with aria-label 'Delete redirect from <path>'. Compare DomainsScreen.tsx:153-160 which does confirm. Searched: 'handleDelete', 'confirm', 'window.confirm', 'ConfirmDialog'.
ux.fix: Confirm, naming the rule being removed and what breaks ('/old-pricing will start returning 404'). An undo window on the row would be better still.

ux.purpose: Configure the whole site — identity, SEO, distribution and plumbing — from one place.
ux.finding: 'Delete' on a form submission permanently destroys a customer's message on the first click — no confirm, no undo, no trash. The row sits inline with 'mark read' and 'mark spam', which are reversible, so the destructive action is presented at the same weight as the safe ones. This is third-party data the site owner is custodian of, not editor state.
ux.evidence: FormsScreen.tsx:153-169 handleDelete -> forms.deleteSubmission.mutate({ id }) then refetch; the trigger at :364-366 is a ghost Button labelled 'Delete' beside the status actions. Searched: 'deleteSubmission', 'handleDelete', 'confirm', 'archive'.
ux.fix: Confirm it, or make it an archive with a restore path. Never put an irreversible delete of someone else's data one click deep next to reversible state toggles.

ux.purpose: Configure the whole site — identity, SEO, distribution and plumbing — from one place.
ux.task: Restore an earlier version of my site
ux.finding: Half of Settings is inside version history and half is outside it, and nothing says which. General, SEO, Analytics and Custom code write through the composer, so they are recorded in undo and captured in every saved version. Redirects, Headers, Localization, Domains, Forms and Webhooks write straight to the server and are invisible to both. A user who restores a version gets their SEO and custom code back and silently keeps the redirects and headers from the state they were trying to leave — with the restore banner assuring them 'nothing is lost'.
ux.evidence: SettingsTab.tsx:581-624 handleSave — screenSaveHandlerRef path skips composer.saveProject() entirely ('it would silently drop Redirects/Headers/Localization fields'); the composer path flushes into composer state, which HistoryManager.ts:194-233 records and VersionTimelineManager captures. Server writers: RedirectsScreen.tsx:160, HeadersScreen.tsx:94, LocalizationScreen.tsx:128, DomainsScreen.tsx:135, WebhooksScreen.tsx:115. The reassurance is VersionHistoryPanel.tsx:365-367 'Your current work is saved first — nothing is lost.' Searched: 'registerSaveHandler', 'saveProject', 'setProjectSettings', 'restoreVersion'.
ux.fix: Say what a version covers, on the restore confirm and on the sections it excludes ('Redirects are not part of version history'). Longer term, bring server-backed site config into the same snapshot.

ux.purpose: Configure the whole site — identity, SEO, distribution and plumbing — from one place.
ux.task: Know which section I am in
ux.finding: Drilling into a section stacks three headers that all say the same word. The panel header retitles itself to the section ('Redirects' + its subtitle), the drill-in header below it renders '← Back to Settings' plus a breadcrumb 'PLUMBING / Redirects', and the screen's own first block is a Section heading 'Redirects'. Three headings, two back-affordances (breadcrumb and back button), one destination — in a surface whose entire content is a form.
ux.evidence: SettingsTab.tsx:803-806 PanelFrame.Header title={isRoot ? 'Settings' : current.title} subtitle={current.subtitle}; :869-877 DrillInHeader title/parentName/breadcrumb; DrillInHeader.tsx:122-170 renders the back button AND the breadcrumb. The screens then add their own: RedirectsScreen.tsx:230, HeadersScreen.tsx:130, LocalizationScreen.tsx:174, FormsScreen.tsx:208, DomainsScreen.tsx:198. Searched: '<Section title=', 'DrillInHeader', 'PanelFrame.Header', 'breadcrumb'.
ux.fix: One header per screen. Keep the panel header as the section title with a single back control; let the screens start at their first field or at a genuinely different sub-heading.

ux.purpose: Configure the whole site — identity, SEO, distribution and plumbing — from one place.
ux.finding: Two Save buttons are live at once for the same edit. Headers and Localization each render their own primary ('Save headers' / 'Save locales') at the bottom of the form AND register with the central savebar, which slides up as soon as the form is dirty with its own 'Save'. The two are identical in effect, adjacent on screen, and differently labelled — so the user has to guess whether one saves the section and the other saves everything.
ux.evidence: HeadersScreen.tsx:268-280 'Save headers' Button + :119 comment that it also registers with the savebar; LocalizationScreen.tsx:288-305 'Save locales' + :163 the registration comment; SettingsTab.tsx:882-896 the savebar with its Discard/Save pair; :707-711 registerSaveHandler routes the savebar's Save into the same screen handler. Searched: 'registerSaveHandler', 'handleSave', 'bd-set-savebar'.
ux.fix: One Save, in one place. If a section genuinely needs its own inline commit, the savebar should not appear for it.

ux.purpose: Configure the whole site — identity, SEO, distribution and plumbing — from one place.
ux.finding: Four different confirmation idioms coexist inside one tab, and three destructive actions have none. Domains uses the browser's native window.confirm — a modal the editor cannot style, that blocks the whole app and reads as a page-level alert. Webhooks uses an inline confirm band with its own state. The tab's own discard guard uses the chrome ConfirmDialog. Redirects, Forms and Localization delete with nothing at all. A user cannot learn what 'delete' means here because it means five things.
ux.evidence: DomainsScreen.tsx:153-160 window.confirm(...); WebhooksScreen.tsx:79 confirming state + :266-290 the inline bands; SettingsTab.tsx:903-964 ConfirmDialog tone='destructive'; no confirm in RedirectsScreen.tsx:160, FormsScreen.tsx:153, LocalizationScreen.tsx:114. Searched across screens/: 'confirm', 'Confirm', 'window.confirm', 'Delete', 'Remove'.
ux.fix: One destructive-confirm pattern for the whole tab, stating the object and the consequence, and no browser-native dialogs anywhere in the editor.

ux.purpose: Configure the whole site — identity, SEO, distribution and plumbing — from one place.
ux.task: Know whether my change is saved
ux.finding: The savebar is the same in every section, but the sections are not: General / SEO / Analytics / Custom code buffer edits and commit on Save; Redirects / Headers / Localization write on the savebar's Save through their own server path; Domains, Forms and Webhooks write IMMEDIATELY on their own buttons and never make the savebar dirty. So the same bar reading '0 unsaved' means 'nothing typed' on one screen and 'already committed to the server' on another, and the user has no way to tell which kind of screen they are on. The counter is also always 0 or 1 — it says '1 unsaved' whether the user changed one field or twelve.
ux.evidence: SettingsTab.tsx:878-897 the savebar renders unconditionally inside any mounted section; :595-598 handleScreenDirty sets dirtyCount to `dirty ? 1 : 0`; :581-624 handleSave branches on screenSaveHandlerRef vs composer.saveProject. Immediate writers: DomainsScreen.tsx:135-160, FormsScreen.tsx:140-169, WebhooksScreen.tsx:115-150. Searched: 'dirtyCount', 'registerSaveHandler', 'registerFlushHandler', 'bd-set-savebar'.
ux.fix: Make the commit model visible: either every section buffers and commits through the savebar, or a section that writes immediately says so and does not render the bar. Count the actual changed fields.

ux.purpose: Configure the whole site — identity, SEO, distribution and plumbing — from one place.
ux.task: Find the setting I came for
ux.finding: Thirteen sections in three groups labelled SITE / DISTRIBUTION / PLUMBING, plus a WORKSPACE group whose rows leave the app — and no search. 'PLUMBING' is an implementer's word, and the grouping puts Analytics under DISTRIBUTION and Forms under PLUMBING, which is not where a user looks for either. The one section a user is most likely to open by name, 'Branding', contains no settings at all: it is a signpost listing five fields and where they really live.
ux.evidence: SettingsTab.tsx:75-98 the NAV array and GROUP_LABELS; :148-154 BRANDING_FIELD_MAP + :161-211 BrandingSection, which renders only 'Open →' jumps and an 'Open Palette →' button; :120-123 WORKSPACE_LINKS open dashboard URLs in a new tab. Grep for 'search' in SettingsTab.tsx returns only the SEO subtitle string. Searched: 'search', 'filter', 'NAV', 'GROUP_LABELS'.
ux.fix: Add a filter over section names and field labels. Rename the groups for the user's vocabulary, and either give Branding real fields or fold its five signposts into the sections that own them.

ux.purpose: Configure the whole site — identity, SEO, distribution and plumbing — from one place.
ux.task: See what Custom code would give me
ux.finding: On a starter plan, two nav rows carry a 'Pro' badge and still drill in — full push animation — to land on a generic card: 'Available in Pro / Upgrade your plan to unlock this feature.' It never says what the feature is or does, so the upgrade decision is asked for with no information. The only forward move opens the billing page in a new browser tab, and the only backward move is the drill-in back button.
ux.evidence: SettingsTab.tsx:625-628 renderContent -> <LockedScreen variant={requiredPlan}/>; LockedScreen.tsx:53-67 renders a PRO badge, 'Available in Pro' and the default message 'Upgrade your plan to unlock this feature.'; :41-51 handleUpgrade -> window.open(billing, '_blank'). types.ts:70-73 SCREEN_PLAN_REQUIREMENTS gates custom-code and integrations. Searched: 'LockedScreen', 'isScreenLocked', 'SCREEN_PLAN_REQUIREMENTS', 'message'.
ux.fix: Show the real screen with its controls disabled and the value visible, or pass a per-screen message that says what is behind the gate. A locked door with no label is indistinguishable from a broken one.

ux.screen: Settings › General vs Pages › Page settings
ux.purpose: Configure the whole site — identity, SEO, distribution and plumbing — from one place.
ux.task: Set the title people see when this page is shared
ux.finding: SEO lives in two places with no cross-reference: a site-level SEO section in Settings and a per-page SEO/Social drawer under Pages, each with its own unsaved-changes guard and its own save. The site-level screen's own copy has already had to be corrected once because it claimed to set a default that page settings always override. A user editing social share text has to know which of the two wins before they can tell whether their edit did anything.
ux.evidence: SettingsTab.tsx:79 the 'seo' nav row -> SeoScreen.tsx:76 'Site SEO'; the per-page surface is sidebar/tabs/pages/page-settings/ (SeoTab.tsx, SocialTab.tsx, AdvancedTab.tsx) with its own UnsavedWarningModal.tsx and PageSettingsDrawer.tsx. ProjectSettingsModal.tsx:232-241 carries the correction: 'Page titles come from each page's own SEO settings.' Searched: 'SeoScreen', 'SeoTab', 'page-settings', 'og:'.
ux.fix: Show the resolution on both screens — the site default with 'overridden on N pages', and the page field with 'site default: …'. Two editors for one output need to name each other.

ux.purpose: Configure the whole site — identity, SEO, distribution and plumbing — from one place.
ux.task: Get my site out / manage the team
ux.finding: One nav list mixes three kinds of destination with only one of them labelled. Most rows drill into an in-place form. 'Export' drills into a section whose entire content is a button that opens a modal exporter somewhere else. 'Members' and 'Billing' are anchors that leave for the dashboard in a new tab — flagged by a small 'opens dashboard ↗' hint on the group header and an '↗' glyph, but sitting in the same row shape as everything above them.
ux.evidence: SettingsTab.tsx:736-750 renderContent 'export' case — a Section with one 'Open exporter' Button emitting UI_TOGGLE_EXPORTER; :772-786 renderWorkspaceLink renders <a target="_blank"> with the same bd-set-snav-row class as the in-tab rows; :840-843 the WORKSPACE group hint. Searched: 'renderWorkspaceLink', 'WORKSPACE_LINKS', 'UI_TOGGLE_EXPORTER', 'target="_blank"'.
ux.fix: Give leaving-the-app rows a different row shape, and either put the exporter's options in the Export section or make the nav row open the exporter directly instead of costing a drill-in to reach one button.
